references.engineTypes: @nilvn/engine type declarations (PluginContext, the capability interfaces, EngineHooks)

fields.name: id
fields.desc: Stable reverse-DNS id (app.nilvn.textfx). The enabled-set / [use] / i18n-namespace key.

fields.name: name
fields.desc: Display name as an i18n id resolved through `messages` (plugin.<slug>.name; slug = the last id segment by convention — a plugin’s messages are its own, so two plugins never clash).

fields.name: engine
fields.desc: Engine compatibility range — subset: `*`, `1.2.3`, `^1.2`, `~1.2.3`, `>=0.14 <1`, `a || b`. Absent = any.

fields.name: dependencies
fields.desc: Other plugins this one needs; activated first. Missing / incompatible / cyclic → the plugin is blocked with a diagnostic.

fields.name: contributes
fields.desc: Contributions per extension point (see `extensionPoints`). Unknown keys are ignored with a warning.

fields.name: permissions
fields.desc: Capabilities requested from the `permissions` catalog. Only these (as granted by the host) become context objects.

fields.name: activation
fields.desc: When the runtime half activates: on enable (default), at its first command, or only through enablePlugin / setPlugins.

fields.name: reload
fields.desc: Hot-plug policy (default hot). `restart` = the host must reload the editor after a toggle.

fields.name: entries
fields.desc: Module entries relative to plugin.json. No engine entry = a pure editor plugin; no editor entry = runtime only.

fields.name: styles
fields.desc: Stylesheets relative to plugin.json, injected while active and removed on deactivate.

fields.name: assets
fields.desc: Resource files relative to plugin.json (no ".."): the complete list an exporter copies, and the only paths ctx.asset() resolves.

fields.name: messages
fields.desc: The plugin’s own UI-chrome strings; `ctx.t(id)` resolves them in the work language.

fields.name: authorUsage
fields.desc: Author-facing usage lines (how to trigger the plugin in an AuthoringDoc); tools prefer these over deriving from contributes.

fields.name: apiVersion
fields.desc: Plugin contract version this manifest targets (current: 2); a newer one is rejected.

contributes.name: commands
contributes.desc: Script commands `[name …]` with typed params (drives the editor insert form and the authoring lint); ifFalse: 'skip' (default) | 'handle' sets what a false trailing if= does.

contributes.name: objectKinds
contributes.desc: Addressable stage-object kinds the plugin adds.

contributes.name: effects
contributes.desc: Retargetable effects bound to kinds via appliesToKinds.

contributes.name: hooks
contributes.desc: Engine hook names the runtime half listens to (introspection).

contributes.name: saveSlice
contributes.desc: The plugin owns a SaveState.ext[id] slice (needs the save.slice permission); version = the slice shape version (default 1), equal to the module stateVersion.

contributes.name: keybindings
contributes.desc: Keys in the engine's key table (needs input.keys): default in the [keys] format ('w', 'Ctrl+S', a list, false); when = playing (default) | always. A default already bound elsewhere stays unbound with a diagnostic; the author moves it with [keys.<short name or id>] <id> = …, the player in the settings screen.

contributes.name: panels
contributes.desc: Editor manager panels the host renders a tab + container for.

contributes.name: nodeKinds
contributes.desc: IR node kinds the editor half owns (forms + inert flag while disabled).

contributes.name: config
contributes.desc: Plugin settings: { key, type, default, label, options?, items?, min?, max?, step?, scope? } (type list = a TOML array, author scope only). The author sets them in the config file’s [plugins.<id>] table (short first-party names work) or the studio; the plugin reads ctx.config.get(key). scope = "player" rows also appear in the in-game settings panel and persist per work (the author’s value is the default). Unknown author keys are one diagnostic.

contributes.name: menuItems
contributes.desc: { id, label (i18n id) } — entries in the in-game system menu, shown while playing; the module wires each with ctx.screen.menuItem(id, onSelect) (needs ui.screen).

contributes.name: titleItems
contributes.desc: { id, label } — buttons on the title page, wired with ctx.screen.titleItem(id, onSelect) (needs ui.screen).

contributes.name: hud
contributes.desc: { id, slot?: top-left | top-right | bottom-left | bottom-right } — a widget container in a stage corner, shown while playing: ctx.screen.hud(id) (needs ui.screen).

contributes.name: actorFields
contributes.desc: { key, type, label? } — fields an actor declaration may carry for this plugin ([actors.<id>] key = … / [actor id key=…]); the engine files them under the actor’s ext[pluginId] and the plugin reads ctx.actorField(actorId, key).

contributes.name: services
contributes.desc: { id, version } — services this plugin offers other plugins, provided with ctx.services.provide(id, api). A consumer lists this plugin in its dependencies and calls ctx.services.get(thisId, id, range?).

contributes.name: themeTokens
contributes.desc: { name, default, label? } — the plugin’s own theme tokens, named <short name>-… (weather-drop for com.example.weather). While the plugin is active the default sits on the stage root as --nilvn-<name>; a work’s [theme] / [theme …] sets it like an engine token, and the plugin’s CSS reads var(--nilvn-<name>).

extensionPoints.description: Script commands `[name …]` (CommandSchema drives the insert form).
Inline text effects `{name:text}`.
Addressable stage-object kinds.
Retargetable effects bound to kinds via appliesToKinds.
Engine hook names the runtime half listens to (introspection; the module is authoritative).
Declares a SaveState.ext slice owned by this plugin.
Plugin settings (ConfigFieldSchema[]): the config file’s [plugins.<id>] table and ctx.config at runtime; scope = player rows also appear in the in-game settings panel and persist per work.
Entries in the in-game system menu (wired with ctx.screen.menuItem; needs ui.screen).
Buttons on the title page (ctx.screen.titleItem; needs ui.screen).
Persistent widgets in a stage corner while playing (ctx.screen.hud; needs ui.screen).
Fields an actor declaration may carry for this plugin ([actors.<id>] / [actor …]), reached as ctx.actorField(actorId, key).
Keyboard bindings in the engine’s key table (id, default key, label, when); handled through ctx.input.on (needs input.keys), rebindable by the player.
Services this plugin offers other plugins (id + semver version), provided through ctx.services.provide; a consumer lists the provider in dependencies and calls ctx.services.get.
The plugin’s own theme tokens (--nilvn-<short>-*) with their defaults: set by the work’s [theme] like the engine’s, read by the plugin’s styles and ctx.theme.
Named renderer layers.
Manager panels (the editor renders the host; the plugin fills it).
IR node kinds this plugin owns (forms + inert flag while disabled).
Stage overlay tools (modal takeovers of the stage).
Buttons on a dialogue line’s action bar.
Sections in an on-stage object’s context menu.
Draggable editor windows.
Insert-palette categories and entries.
Extra timeline lanes.
Steps in the export pipeline.
Project menu entries.
Selected-object inspector sections.
AI slots (roadmap §6).
AI providers (roadmap §6).

CommandSchema.name: label
CommandSchema.desc: i18n id (plugin messages) for the editor insert menu.

CommandSchema.name: category
CommandSchema.desc: Where the editor files the command.

CommandSchema.name: hint
CommandSchema.desc: One-line help (an i18n id or text).

CommandSchema.name: icon
CommandSchema.desc: An emoji for the insert menu.

CommandSchema.name: ifFalse
CommandSchema.desc: What a false trailing if= does (default skip; handle = the command runs with ctx.cond === false).

ParamSchema.name: key
ParamSchema.desc: The parameter name: [cmd key=value]. A positional param is still named here (forms, lint) but arrives in ctx.args[positional].

ParamSchema.name: type
ParamSchema.desc: One of `schemas.paramTypes` (asset / actor / face / … drive editor pickers).

ParamSchema.name: positional
ParamSchema.desc: The argument index (0, 1, …): the value is written as a bare word at that position ([weather rain] → ctx.args[0]) instead of key=value.

ParamSchema.name: required
ParamSchema.desc: The editor and the authoring lint require it; the runtime does not check.

ParamSchema.name: default
ParamSchema.desc: Shown and used by the editor; the command still reads its own fallback (str(key, def) / num(key, def)).

ParamSchema.name: options
ParamSchema.desc: The choices of an enum (label = i18n id).

ParamSchema.name: list
ParamSchema.desc: A positional holding several whitespace-separated values.

ParamSchema.name: advanced
ParamSchema.desc: Folded behind "advanced" in the editor form.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: key
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: The setting: ctx.config.get(key), [plugins.<id>] key = … in the config.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: label
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: i18n id (plugin messages) — the settings row / studio form.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: type
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: One of `schemas.configTypes`. In the settings screen: boolean → On / Off, number with min + max → a slider, enum → buttons, anything else → a text field. list (config only, author scope only) is a TOML array; ctx.config.get returns an array.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: default
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: The value until the author or player sets one (ctx.config.get returns it). A list’s default is an array.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: min / max / step
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: Number range: values are clamped into it; a player row needs min and max to render as a slider.

ConfigFieldSchema.name: scope
ConfigFieldSchema.desc: author (default): the config file only; player: also a row in the game’s settings screen, persisted per work (the author’s value is the default). A list is author-only.

KeybindingDef.name: id
KeybindingDef.desc: Local to the plugin; the key table calls it <plugin id>:<id>, the author’s override is [keys.<short name or id>] <id> = …, and ctx.input.on(id, fn) handles it.

KeybindingDef.name: default
KeybindingDef.desc: The [keys] format: "w", "Ctrl+S", a list, or false (unbound until someone binds it).

KeybindingDef.name: label
KeybindingDef.desc: i18n id (plugin messages) for the settings screen’s key list (default: the id).

KeybindingDef.name: when
KeybindingDef.desc: playing (default): while the story plays with no system menu, panel or plugin screen open. always: also on the title and ending pages and while a plugin screen is open — never while a system menu panel is open or a text field has focus. For a title-only key, use always and check ctx.session in the handler.

MenuItemDef.name: id
MenuItemDef.desc: Wired with ctx.screen.menuItem(id, onSelect) (titleItems: titleItem). The menu closes before onSelect runs; onSelect gets no arguments.

MenuItemDef.name: when
MenuItemDef.desc: Deprecated and ignored (a validator warning): the system menu only opens while playing. A title-page entry is a titleItems entry.

HudDef.name: id
HudDef.desc: ctx.screen.hud(id) returns the corner container (shown only while playing).

ActorFieldDef.name: key
ActorFieldDef.desc: [actors.<id>] key = … / [actor … key=…]; read with ctx.actorField(actorId, key).

ServiceDef.name: id
ServiceDef.desc: Local to the plugin (letters, digits, - and _); consumers ask for (plugin id, id).

ServiceDef.name: version
ServiceDef.desc: The service interface’s own semver version ("1.0.0"); a consumer’s range is checked against it.

ThemeTokenDef.name: name
ThemeTokenDef.desc: Lower-case words joined by dashes, starting with the plugin’s short name and a dash (the id’s last segment: weather- for com.example.weather); the custom property is --nilvn-<name>. May not reuse an engine token or another active plugin’s.

ThemeTokenDef.name: default
ThemeTokenDef.desc: One CSS value (no ; { }); may reference other tokens, e.g. var(--nilvn-accent).

TextEffectDef.name: name
TextEffectDef.desc: Used inline as {name:text}; implemented in the module’s textEffects.

ObjectKindSchema.name: transformable
ObjectKindSchema.desc: Whether it takes the transform schema.

EffectSchema.name: name
EffectSchema.desc: The effect, implemented in the module’s effects.

EffectSchema.name: command
EffectSchema.desc: The command that applies it (its CommandSchema drives the form).

EffectSchema.name: targetParams / fanout / hint / icon
EffectSchema.desc: Editor wiring: params pointing the command at the chosen object; an enum param to expand into one entry per option.

permissions.description: Read stage objects: hasObject / getProp / getBand / getFace / hasChar / charFace / snapshot.
Stage read + every Renderer write verb, applyEffect, and keyframe choreography (playFrames / startLoop / stopLoop).
A named renderer layer (weather / masks).
playTrack / stopTrack / stopAllTracks / playSe, channel volumes and voicePlaying.
A specific audio bus.
Microphone capture (host-mediated).
Read script variables.
Read + write script variables.
Own a SaveState.ext slice (saveState / restoreState are called).
saveState / restoreState / restart, the work save key and build info.
Text speed, channel volumes, language switching, resolveText.
The dialogue backlog and voice replay by ref.
A–B replay segments: list / play / end / seen signals.
A host container inside the stage root (removed on dispose).
Full-stage screens over the story, entries in the system menu and on the title page, HUD widgets (the menuItems / titleItems / hud contributions).
In-engine confirm / alert boxes and toasts (never the browser’s).
A manager panel host in the editor.
A draggable editor window.
Editor toasts.
The selected-object inspector panel.
Read the open project (IR) and editor state.
Mutate the project through the editor (undoable).
Resolve project assets.
Import / replace project assets.
Native file picker (host-mediated).
Files under the project directory (host-mediated).
Network access to one origin (host-mediated; third-party default-deny).
Clipboard read / write.
setTimeout / setInterval / requestAnimationFrame, cleared on dispose.
Keyboard bindings declared in contributes.keybindings, handled through ctx.input.on; the player can rebind them in the settings.
A key-value store namespaced per work and plugin (async, JSON values) — the engine’s SaveStore.
Text generation through the configured provider.
Image generation.
Audio / voice generation.
Code generation (plugins from natural language).
Read the authoring context handed to AI slots.

module.name: permissions
module.desc: Only for a module with no plugin.json (a bare [use ./x.js] or a host-registered module). With a manifest, write permissions there only; if both are given and their engine-side sets differ, the manifest wins with a diagnostic.

module.name: version / dependencies / activation / reload
module.desc: Inline fallbacks for module-only plugins ([use ./x.js]); a manifest wins.

module.name: textEffects
module.type: Record<name, (span: TextSpan, index, ctx: PluginContext) => void>
module.desc: Inline text effects; `span.addClass` is the only verb.

module.name: objectKinds
module.desc: Runtime kind contracts: `transformable` + `recordable` channels — standard channel NAMES (x / y / scale / rotation / opacity / visible / face / band) or custom RecordableProp descriptors.

module.name: effects
module.desc: Effects run with the OWNER plugin’s context.

module.name: hooks
module.desc: onReady / onSessionChange(state, prev) / onLabel(label) / onDialogue / onDialogueDone / onReveal / onChoices / onChoose / onCommand / onEnd / onSaved(state) / onRestored(state) / onSettingsChange(key, value) / onVarChange(name, value) / onPreload(done, total, ref) / onError — each receives the plugin context last.

module.name: activate(ctx)
module.desc: Once per activation. Register listeners / timers / layers through ctx so they are released on deactivate. A throw isolates the plugin.

module.name: deactivate(ctx)
module.desc: Before the host disposes everything registered through ctx.

module.name: saveState(ctx) / restoreState(ctx, data)
module.desc: The SaveState.ext[id] slice (needs save.slice); restoreState always receives the current stateVersion shape.

module.name: stateVersion / migrateState(data, from)
module.desc: Slice shape version (default 1). An older saved slice goes through migrateState first; without it, or from a newer version, the slice is dropped with a diagnostic and loading continues.

context.name: id / permissions / lang / session / actors
context.desc: Identity, granted permissions, the work language, where the session is (idle / title / playing / ending — onSessionChange announces each change), the actor table.

context.name: resolve(path)
context.desc: Resource path → URL (aliases / by-ref assets / base URL).

context.name: asset(path)
context.desc: One of the plugin’s own files (listed in manifest assets) → URL: through the package for a carried plugin, relative to plugin.json / the module for a URL-loaded one.

context.name: t(id, params?)
context.desc: In the work language: the author’s [strings] first (a work may rename a plugin’s text), then the plugin’s own `messages`, then the engine chrome catalog; {name} placeholders filled from params.

context.name: report(message, error?)
context.desc: A `plugin` diagnostic attributed to this plugin (never throw over content).

context.name: listen(target, type, fn, opts?)
context.desc: Event listener removed on dispose.

context.name: onDispose(fn)
context.desc: Run on deactivate.

context.name: registerCommand / registerTextEffect / registerEffect / registerKind / on(hook, fn) / addStyle(css)
context.desc: Dynamic registration; all disposable.

context.name: theme
context.desc: Always present: get(token) / all() / onChange(fn) over the work’s `--nilvn-*` theme overrides (THEME_TOKENS has the defaults). Plugin CSS draws with var(--nilvn-…), never colour literals, so it follows the theme.

context.name: config
context.desc: Always present: get(key) / all() / onChange(fn) — this plugin’s settings, resolved schema default ← the author’s [plugins.<id>] value ← the player’s value.

context.name: actorField(actorId, key)
context.desc: Always present: a contributes.actorFields value for that actor (undefined when absent).

context.name: services
context.desc: Always present: provide(id, api) → withdraw() offers a declared contributes.services entry (each function of api becomes a method); get(pluginId, serviceId, range?) → the provider’s methods, every one async, arguments and results structured-cloned both ways (data only, no functions or DOM). get needs the provider in dependencies; it is undefined when the range does not match or nothing is provided, and a call after the provider withdrew rejects.

context.name: storage
context.desc: storage.local: get / set / remove / keys — a key-value store namespaced per work and plugin (async, JSON values), backed by the engine’s SaveStore.

context.name: screen
context.desc: ui.screen: open(id, title, render) → Promise resolved when that screen closes (any way) / close(id?) / isOpen(id?) full-stage screens in the engine’s panel chrome; menuItem(id, onSelect) / titleItem(id, onSelect) wire contributes.menuItems / titleItems; hud(id) → the contributes.hud container. All released on dispose.

context.name: dialog
context.desc: ui.dialog: confirm(message) → Promise<boolean>, alert(message), prompt(message, { default?, maxlength?, pattern?, type?: text | number, min?, max?, step?, lines? }) → Promise<string | null>, toast(message) — the engine’s own boxes, never the browser’s.

context.name: stage
context.desc: stage.read: hasObject / getProp / getBand / getFace / hasChar / charFace / snapshot. stage.write adds every Renderer write verb + applyEffect / showActor / playFrames / stopFrames / startLoop / stopLoop / runningLoops (write verbs are reporting stubs under stage.read only). playFrames / startLoop / stopLoop accept the keyframe WIRE forms (`obj#t:ch=v;…|…`, `t:ch=v;…`, `ch=v,…`) as well as decoded tracks — the engine owns the codec.

context.name: audio
context.desc: audio.play: playTrack / stopTrack / stopAllTracks / playSe / volume(channel) / voicePlaying.

context.name: vars
context.desc: vars.read: get / has / all over the plugin’s own variables (keys without the prefix), global(name) for an author variable, namespace; vars.write adds set (a stub without it). They are stored under the full id (namespace, - → _: com.example.weather.intensity) — what saves hold and what always works in scripts. Scripts may also use the short prefix (a third-party id’s last segment: weather.intensity) while no other active plugin shares it; plugins that share one all lose it, each with a diagnostic.

context.name: input
context.desc: input.keys: on(id, fn) runs fn when a contributes.keybindings binding is pressed (auto-repeat excluded); released on dispose. label(id) is the key it has now as the settings screen shows it ("F", "Ctrl+S"; "" when unbound).

context.name: saves
context.desc: session.save: saveState / restoreState / restart / saveKey / buildInfo.

context.name: settings
context.desc: session.settings: textSpeed, getVolume / setVolume, lang / languages / languageName / setLanguage / onLanguageChange, resolveText.

context.name: backlog
context.desc: session.backlog: entries / replayVoice.

context.name: replay
context.desc: session.replay: list / isReplaying / play / end / fireSeen / onSeen / onEnd.

context.name: ui
context.desc: ui.layer: layer(className) → a host container in the stage root; onStage(type, fn) for stage input. Both released on dispose.

context.name: timer
context.desc: timer: setTimeout / setInterval / requestAnimationFrame and their clears; all cleared on dispose.

commandContext.name: name / args / params / raw
commandContext.desc: The parsed tag, without its trailing `if=` (the engine splits and evaluates it).

commandContext.name: cond
commandContext.desc: The tag's `if=`: true when absent or holding. A false one skips the command unless its CommandSchema declares ifFalse: 'handle' — then the command runs with cond === false and decides what "not present" means.

commandContext.name: condExpr
commandContext.desc: For an ifFalse: 'handle' command only: the if= expression as written. Hand it to the stage (showSprite’s spec.if) and the engine re-evaluates it on every variable change — the sprite is drawn and clickable only while it holds.

commandContext.name: str(keyOrIndex, def?) / num(keyOrIndex, def?) / numOpt(keyOrIndex)
commandContext.desc: Argument accessors (positional index or named key); numOpt yields undefined for an absent / non-numeric param instead of a default.

commandContext.name: plugin
commandContext.desc: The owning plugin’s capability context — the ONLY way to the stage / audio / vars.

signatures.name: stage.setBackground
signatures.desc: `url` resolved (`ctx.resolve` / `ctx.asset`); `ref` = the unresolved path a save should keep.

signatures.name: stage.showChar / showActor
signatures.type: (id, url, { at?, fade?, face?, ref?, y?, scale?, rotation? }) / (id, face?, { at?, fade?, src?, y?, scale?, rotation? }) => Promise<void>
signatures.desc: `showChar` shows a raw image as character `id`; prefer `showActor`, which goes through the actor table like `[char]`.

signatures.name: stage.showSprite
signatures.desc: `spec`: `{ url, ref?, frames, fps, loop, at?, height?, y?, scale?, rotation?, onclick?, if? }` — `url` is the resolved single-row sheet, `frames` / `fps` its frame count and rate, `loop` must be given (`[sprite]` defaults it to true, the call does not), `height` a percentage of the stage height (default 30), `onclick` script commands, `if` a live condition (see `condExpr`). The object is `sprite:<id>`.

signatures.name: stage.getProp / setProp
signatures.desc: `prop` is one of `x` `y` (pixels, or `"12%"` of the object's own box) `scale` `rotation` (degrees) `opacity` `visible` `zIndex`, and on the camera `hue` `invert` `saturate` `brightness` `contrast` `grayscale`.

signatures.name: stage.animate
signatures.type: (objId, frames, { durationSec, easing?, iterations?, compose?, key?, commit? }) => Promise<void>
signatures.desc: `frames`: an array of partial transforms, each with an optional `offset` (0..1) and `easing`; `compose: 'offset'` adds to the resting value instead of replacing it. Resolves at the end, or when stopped. The resting value is untouched — `get` reads the value before, and the object returns to it — unless `commit: true` (an `absolute`, finite animation), which makes the last frame the resting pose that `get` reads and a save keeps. `key` names the animation on its object: a second one with the same key replaces the first, so re-applying an effect never stacks. `key` and `commit` *(since 0.19.0)*.

signatures.name: stage.stopAnimations
signatures.desc: Stops what `animate` started on the object — all, or the one with `key` — and the object returns to its resting pose; an `iterations: Infinity` animation runs until then. Show / hide fades and keyframe loops are not touched. An animation is not part of a save: a loop that must survive one is `startLoop`. *(since 0.19.0)*

signatures.name: stage.fadeScreen / transitionScreen / flash
signatures.type: (to, sec, color = '#000') / (to, sec, { shape?, dir?, color?, mask?, softness? }) / (color, durationSec) => Promise<void>

signatures.name: stage.applyEffect
signatures.desc: Runs a registered effect on an object; `params` is a `Record<string, string>`.

signatures.name: stage.playFrames / stopFrames / startLoop / stopLoop / runningLoops
signatures.type: (durationSec, tracks) / () / (objId, durationSec, entry, body, intoEase?, bridge?) / (objId, exit, outEase?) / ()
signatures.desc: Keyframe playback; `tracks` / `entry` / `body` / `exit` take the keyframe wire strings or decoded objects.

signatures.name: effect handle
signatures.type: id, kind, get(prop), set(prop, value), animate(frames, opts), stopAnimations(key?), getBand(), setBand(band), getFace(), setFace(face)
signatures.desc: What apply(handle, params, ctx) receives, bound to one object. `id` is the full object id (`character:yuki`), `kind` its kind (`character`); the rest are the stage verbs above without the `objId`, and nothing else.

signatures.name: hook onChoices
signatures.type: `items` (`{ text, textKey?, target, cond?, disabled? }[]`, the shown ones), `handles` (`ChoiceHandle[]`: `index`, `addClass(name)`, `setVar(name, value)`)

signatures.name: write verb misuse
signatures.desc: Every write verb that returns a promise resolves when its fade or animation ends; a verb called with arguments it cannot use reports a diagnostic against your plugin and does nothing — it never throws back into your code.

lifecycle: register(manifest / module) → validate (id grammar · apiVersion · engine range · dependencies · permission catalog) → activate(ctx) → running → deactivate(ctx) → dispose
Every contribution and resource registered through ctx is released on deactivate; a plugin must not hold globals.
activate() may be async; a rejection or throw isolates the plugin (its commands become no-ops, one diagnostic).
N consecutive command failures (default 3) isolate the plugin; one success resets the count.
reload = saveState slice → deactivate → (re-import cache-busted for path plugins) → activate → restoreState; any failure rolls back to the previous module.
activation.engine: eager (default) | onCommand (first execution of one of its commands) | manual (enablePlugin / setPlugins only).
A running engine (finished game) never hot-swaps its command set; the editor toggles in edit mode and rebuilds the preview per run.

A script package carries a third-party plugin under plugins/<id>/ with every file in its by-ref asset table (nilvn.json plugins[].entry = the plugin.json); the engine imports the module from the URL the package loader serves, so the engine entry must be one self-contained ES module (no relative imports). A carried plugin reloads in place (no re-import).
proxyRules: Capability methods are async or pure; return values and parameters must be structured-cloneable.
No DOM handles cross the boundary — TextSpan / ChoiceHandle / StageObjectHandle are proxyable handle objects (index / id + methods).
A denied capability is undefined on the context, never an exception; stage write verbs under stage.read only are reporting stubs.
Third-party plugins default-deny net:* and fs.*; those permissions are reserved until the host mediates them.

In a sandbox, synchronous reads of live state become async: stage hasObject / getProp / getBand / getFace / hasChar / charFace / snapshot / runningLoops, saves.saveState, settings.resolveText, backlog.entries. Reads of slow-changing data (vars, theme, config, lang, session, actors, resolve, asset, t, volumes) are served from a host-pushed mirror and stay synchronous.
ctx.services calls are async both ways and structured-clone their arguments and results already, so a service interface needs no change to cross a sandbox.

Same-realm only (unavailable in a sandbox, declarative equivalents to come): ctx.listen, ui.layer / ui.onStage, the HTMLElement of screen.open render and screen.hud, custom RecordableProp descriptors (standard channel names are fine), showChar opts.faceUrl (use showActor).

module.name: panels
module.desc: Builders for contributes.panels; the host renders the tab + container.

module.name: stageTool / objectMenuSection / lineActions
module.desc: Deep integrations for contributes.stageTools / objectMenu / lineActions (full editor context).

context.name: id / permissions
context.desc: Identity and the granted editor-side permissions.

context.name: state
context.desc: project.read: the open project and selection.

context.name: commit(name, mutate, opts?) / run(op)
context.desc: project.commit: change the project through the editor command surface (a named undoable transaction, or a registry op with serializable params); nothing else writes.

context.name: assets
context.desc: assets.read (imports also need assets.write).

context.name: refresh()
context.desc: Any ui.*: repaint the editor.

context.name: toast(message, kind?)
context.desc: ui.toast.
